media:group.media:title: Tabular Foundation Models for Data Science Agents
media:group.media:description:
Learn More: https://bit.ly/4j2WLq8
Tabular foundation models use in-context learning to make predictions on new datasets without training a model from scratch. In this short course, built in partnership with Prior Labs and taught by Frank Hutter, Eliott Kalfon, and Tuana Çelik, you'll:
- Make classification, regression, and forecasting predictions with a tabular foundation model - Speed up repeated predictions with KV caching - Interpret predictions to see which features influence them and what drove each one - Build a data science agent that calls a tabular foundation model as a tool when a prediction is needed - Train a tiny tabular foundation model from scratch to see how they are built

entry.title: Stop guessing how to fix your agent

media:group.media:title: Stop guessing how to fix your agent
media:group.media:description:
Learn More: https://bit.ly/4ikf9L0
Traditional software tests confirm that your code is working, but fall short when it comes to testing agents. Evals allow you to measure an agent’s decisions and actions when its failures may not be obvious.
In our new course, Evaluating and Improving Agentic Applications, built in partnership with Arize AI, you’ll take an agent through the full evaluation process, from reading its traces to improving it. Taught by Laurie Voss, Head of Developer Relations at Arize and co-founder of npm.
In this course, you’ll learn how to:
Read your agent’s traces to find recurring failures and turn them into a test set you can rerun after every change. Automate evaluation with code and LLM judges you can rely on. Use your evals to check that every change makes your agent better.
Enroll for free: https://bit.ly/4ikf9L0

entry.title: Agents on longer tasks need more than one loop

media:group.media:title: Agents on longer tasks need more than one loop
media:group.media:description:
Learn More: https://bit.ly/4BuaMVb
An agent that calls tools and decides its next step can complete a task. Making that agent reliable over longer, more complex work takes more: loops that check its output, start a new run each time an event occurs, and help the agent improve from past runs.
In our new short course, Loop Engineering with LangChain Deep Agents, built in collaboration with LangChain and taught by Sydney Runkle, maintainer of Deep Agents at LangChain, and Esmaeil Gargari, you'll learn a framework for four loops around an agent and how to build each one.
In this course, you'll learn how to: - Build an agent loop that calls tools, observes results, and decides what to do next - Add a verification loop that checks the agent’s output and sends feedback for another attempt - Set up an event-driven loop so external events trigger new runs automatically - Use a hill-climbing loop that analyzes traces from many runs to improve the agent’s harness
Enroll Now: https://bit.ly/4BuaMVb

media:group.media:title: 7 AI code review best practices #deeplearningai #qodo
media:group.media:description:
A pull request can look clean and still miss a requirement or hide a security issue. When AI writes more of your code, there is often too much to check by hand.
AI Code Review, built in collaboration with Qodo and taught by Nnenna Ndukwe, walks through 7 review practices with before and after examples. A few of them:
🔍Run the review before you open a pull request 🧑‍💻Use a reviewer that didn’t write the code 📂Give the reviewer task and repository context ⚖️Triage findings by risk 🔁Turn good feedback into reusable standards
💡The key lesson: the context you give your reviewer matters more than which model you use.
🛠️You’ll also build your own review agent. Start with a context engine (chunking, embeddings, vector search), then extend it into an ensemble of specialized reviewers.
📌Intermediate, about 1 hour, Python recommended.
👉Enroll now: https://www.deeplearning.ai/courses/ai-code-review
#DeepLearningAI #CodeReview #AIEngineering

entry.title: Learn to build better AI Agents through better context

media:group.media:title: Learn to build better AI Agents through better context
media:group.media:description:
Learn More: https://bit.ly/4yy5iWP
The longer an agent works, the more repeated, contradictory, or stale information builds up in its context. Models perform worse as their context grows, a problem Jeff Huber and his team at Chroma named Context Rot.
In our new course, Context Engineering, taught by Jeff Huber alongside guest speaker Drew Breunig, you'll build agent harnesses from scratch in Python and learn to give agents the right information, in the right format, at the right time.
In this course, you'll learn: - Agentic search: Retrieve data with multiple search tools from different sources. Use traces to improve tool selection through evals. - Context management: Use pruning, compaction, and scratchpads to format the information an agent needs to complete a task. - Agentic memory: Store context from user feedback as reusable memories, retrieve it when a task needs it, and update records across sessions as information changes.
Enroll for free: https://bit.ly/4yy5iWP

entry.title: Building AI Assistants with On-Device Memory

media:group.media:title: Building AI Assistants with On-Device Memory
media:group.media:description:
Learn More: https://bit.ly/4AlVW2n
A cloud-based assistant can remember what it sees, hears, and is told, but only by staying connected and sending that data to a remote server.
In our new short course, Building AI Assistants with On-Device Memory, built in partnership with Qdrant and taught by Dylan Couzon, Developer Experience Engineer at Qdrant, you'll learn to store and search an assistant's memories locally, so nothing has to leave the device.
In this course, you'll learn how to:
- Build a local memory system that stores, retrieves, filters, and forgets text and image memories. - Build an offline assistant that recalls experiences across text, voice, and images. - Teach an AI application to recognize new objects from stored examples without retraining a model. - Run the on-device AI assistant on a local machine, including Mac, Windows, and Linux.
This course also includes our new AI coding lab, so you can practice building with an AI coding agent from the DeepLearning.AI mobile app.
Enroll Now:https://bit.ly/4AlVW2n

entry.title: Full Course: Spec-Driven Development with Coding Agents

media:group.media:title: Full Course: Spec-Driven Development with Coding Agents
media:group.media:description:
Vibe coding is fast, but it often produces code that doesn't match what you asked for. Spec-driven development is the disciplined alternative: write a clear markdown spec defining what to build, and let your coding agent implement it.
Earn your certificate here: https://bit.ly/4hmJc2K
You'll learn to: - Write a project constitution defining mission, tech stack, and roadmap - Plan, implement, and validate features using a spec as the agent's guide - Introduce SDD to a legacy codebase - Package your workflow into an agent skill that's portable across agents and IDEs
Spec-Driven Development with Coding Agents is built in partnership with JetBrains and taught by Paul Everitt, Developer Advocate at JetBrains.
Recommended: basic familiarity with a programming language and experience with LLM-based coding tools.
